# Temple Scroll Column 35 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 35 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**35:1** No person who is unclean from any human impurity shall enter My temple until he has completed his purification.

**35:2** No man who has a bodily discharge, or who has experienced a seminal emission, shall enter My temple.

**35:3** Not until the day he has washed in water and the sun has set — then he may enter on the following day.

**35:4** No blind person shall enter it throughout his lifetime, lest he defile My temple, for I dwell in its midst.

**35:5** No lame person, nor any person with a permanent bodily defect, shall enter and defile My temple.

**35:6** You shall warn all the children of Israel concerning every form of impurity, so that they do not defile My temple.

**35:7** Every man who purifies himself from his discharge shall count seven days for his purification.

**35:8** On the eighth day he shall wash his garments and immerse his entire body in flowing water; then he shall be clean.

**35:9** Once he is clean, he may partake of the holy things, for the holy things are his sustenance.

**35:10** Any man who has not yet completed his days of purification shall not partake of the holy things.

**35:11** He shall not enter My sanctuary until his days of purification are complete.

**35:12** This is so that the children of Israel do not render themselves impure in the midst of their impurity and defile My temple, in which I dwell.

**35:13** Any man who lies with his wife and has a seminal emission shall not enter any part of the temple city for three days.

**35:14** No impure person shall be visible in any part of My temple.

**35:15** You shall station guards at the gates of My temple to prevent any impure person from entering.

**35:16** For My temple is holy, and the place where I have established My name is holy; it shall not be defiled.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 35 codifies purity requirements exceeding standard Pentateuchal legislation. The permanent exclusion of the blind and lame (vv. 4-5) reflects a stricter holiness standard. "Flowing water" renders mayim chayyim. The three-day post-coital exclusion from the temple city (v. 13) extends the Leviticus 15:18 one-day period.*
